newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela may re-offer Bachaquero oil contract.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela may re-offer Bachaquero oil contract.

text.p: Venezuela's state-owned oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) will probably re-offer the Bachaquero southwest oil contract later on Friday after it received no bids from private firms on Friday morning, a spokesman said.
The contract was one of 20 being offered to private firms under Venezuela's third round of operating contracts, where companies receive a sliding fee for reactivating ageing or abandoned oilfields.

"It is very probable we will reoffer the area," said PDVSA exploration and production manager Vincenzo Paglione. "I was a bit surprised there was absolutely no-one. It is an area with small reserves but has great potential for lateral exploration and has a very attractive crude of 44 API."
It was the second contract that has gone unclaimed by companies in a bidding round that has netted more than $2 billion in cash bids so far this week.
Proven reserves in Bachaquero southwest stood at six million barrels, but Paglione said this figure could be increased to 19 million barrels with improved recovery rates.
He said Lagoven would continue producing from the field if no bidders stepped forward. Current production stood at 319 barrels per day.
